web_evidence.title: Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell by Susanna Clarke — Chapter 1: The Library at Hurtfew
web_evidence.note: A sustained excerpt of pages 3–15, reproduced with Bloomsbury's permission, externally narrates the York magicians, Segundus, Honeyfoot, and Norrell and enters characters' thoughts without a participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Jonathan Strange and Mr. Norrell: A Crooked Timber Seminar
web_evidence.note: In her response to the seminar's narrator discussion, Clarke describes the voice as an ordinary nineteenth-century, all-seeing and all-knowing narrator, resolving speculation that it is a participating future character.

web_evidence.title: Fantasy and Realism: Tolkien, the Eucatastrophe, and Fantastic Realism
web_evidence.note: The scholarly analysis quotes Clarke's all-seeing, all-knowing description and explicitly states that the narrator is not a participating character, despite having a personality and making first-person comments.

web_evidence.title: The Basics of Point of View for Fiction Writers
web_evidence.note: The point-of-view analysis explicitly identifies the novel as using an omniscient narrator to manage its large cast and treats its strong narrating personality as third-person omniscience.

web_evidence.title: From the Archives: Fiction Reviews, 1933–2023
web_evidence.note: Kirkus's review characterizes the novel as having a witty, congenial omniscient authorial presence, corroborating a controlling external narrator.

search_log: Searched the verified title and author with excerpt, first chapter, point of view, third person, narrator, omniscient, epistolary, frame narrative, and multiple-narrator terms.
Searched publisher and author domains for an authorized excerpt; the Bloomsbury product and reading-guide pages verified the work but did not themselves provide enough sustained narrative prose.
Opened and assessed the BookBrowse chapter-one excerpt, which reproduces pages 3–15 with explicit permission from Bloomsbury Press.
Searched for explicit whole-book narrator descriptions and opened Jane Friedman's POV analysis and Kirkus's archived review; both identify an omniscient external voice.

Located the Crooked Timber seminar containing Susanna Clarke's response to speculation about the narrator and a University of Regina thesis preserved by Library and Archives Canada that quotes and interprets that response.
Checked Google Books previews and selected-page listings; they verified edition and chapter structure but yielded little accessible prose beyond the stronger opened excerpt.

Ran targeted searches for potentially contrary first-person quotes. These identified q00023 as the gentleman with the thistle-down hair's speech and q00032 as Vinculus's speech; searches for q00003, q00010, and q00078 did not recover sufficient surrounding text for all local attributions.
person_note: The controlling voice is a nonparticipating third-person omniscient narrator with an unusually visible authorial personality. Numerous quotes sustain external access to Norrell, Strange, Childermass, Stephen, and other characters, while the authorized opening excerpt independently shows the same arrangement. The narrator sometimes says I, my readers, or you and I, but q00013, q00069, q00081, and q00102 show that these are intrusions by an authorial observer who continues to narrate the characters externally; they do not make the narrator a participant or create alternating first-person sections. Other first-person material is dialogue, prophecy, verse, quoted thought, or an embedded document. The remaining uncertainty concerns the narrator's precise fictional identity and a few context-clipped quotations, not the controlling narrative person.
